articles.title: Introducing gpt-oss
articles.description: We’re releasing gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b—two state-of-the-art open-weight language models that deliver strong real-world performance at low cost. Available under the flexible Apache 2.0 license, these models outperform similarly sized open models on reasoning tasks, demonstrate strong tool use capabilities, and are optimized for efficient deployment on consumer hardware.
articles.raw_content: We’re releasing gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b—two state-of-the-art open-weight language models that deliver strong real-world performance at low cost. articles.selection_reason: OpenAI releasing state-of-the-art open-weight models under Apache 2.0 is a watershed moment for the open-source AI community.
articles.audience_value: Early access to gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b enables innovators to build, fine-tune, and deploy cutting-edge reasoning models without vendor lock-in.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: OpenAI’s first open-weight release gives innovators a powerful, low-cost foundation for next-generation AI applications and research.

articles.title: OpenAI frontier models and Codex are now available on AWS
articles.description: OpenAI frontier models and Codex are now generally available on AWS, giving enterprises a new path to build with OpenAI through the AWS environments, controls, and procurement workflows they already use. Customers can get started with OpenAI on AWS and move faster from evaluation to production.

articles.selection_reason: OpenAI frontier models and Codex on AWS bridge the gap between leading AI and enterprise infrastructure, a major shift for production deployments.
articles.audience_value: Direct access to OpenAI’s most advanced models via AWS means faster, compliant scaling for innovators building enterprise AI products.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: This partnership removes procurement friction, letting innovators deploy frontier AI at enterprise scale with existing cloud workflows.

articles.title: AMD and OpenAI announce strategic partnership to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs
articles.description: AMD and OpenAI have announced a multi-year partnership to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs, beginning with 1 gigawatt in 2026, to power OpenAI’s next-generation AI infrastructure and accelerate global AI innovation.
articles.raw_content: AMD and OpenAI have announced a multi-year partnership to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs, beginning with 1 gigawatt in 2026, to power OpenAI’s next-generation AI infrastructure and accelerate global AI innovation.
articles.selection_reason: AMD and OpenAI’s 6-gigawatt GPU partnership signals a fundamental shift in AI hardware supply and competition.
articles.audience_value: Understanding this deal is critical for innovators planning infrastructure budgets and model training roadmaps over the next five years.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: This deal reshapes the AI compute landscape, giving innovators an alternative to NVIDIA and influencing future model training economics.

articles.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
articles.description: OpenAI shares findings from the Hugging Face security incident and the steps we’re taking to strengthen AI model security, monitoring, and alignment.
articles.raw_content: OpenAI shares findings from the Hugging Face security incident and the steps we’re taking to strengthen AI model security, monitoring, and alignment.
articles.selection_reason: OpenAI’s deep dive into the Hugging Face security incident provides critical lessons for the entire AI ecosystem on model safety and alignment.
articles.audience_value: Innovators working with open models and third-party infrastructure will gain actionable insights on securing AI deployments against real-world threats.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: The incident reveals systemic risks in AI supply chains, and OpenAI’s findings are a must-read for anyone deploying or distributing models.

articles.title: Advancing science and math with GPT-5.2
articles.description: GPT-5.2 is OpenAI’s strongest model yet for math and science, setting new state-of-the-art results on benchmarks like GPQA Diamond and FrontierMath. This post shows how those gains translate into real research progress, including solving an open theoretical problem and generating reliable mathematical proofs.

This post shows how those gains translate into real research progress, including solving an open theoretical problem and generating reliable mathematical proofs.
articles.selection_reason: GPT-5.2 sets new state-of-the-art on science benchmarks and solves an open theoretical problem, proving AI’s growing role in research.
articles.audience_value: Innovators will see concrete evidence of how frontier models can accelerate mathematical proofs and scientific discovery, guiding their own research agendas.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: GPT-5.2 isn’t just a model update – it’s a demonstration that AI can now contribute to original scientific breakthroughs.
